paragraphs.source_en: Present firstly in the lower altitudes, with the climatic optimum in the 10th millennium BP, the rock art appears on the Tassili Plateau where it develops enormously, both quantitatively and qualitatively.

units.source_en: Present firstly in the lower altitudes, with the climatic optimum in the 10th millennium BP, the rock art appears on the Tassili Plateau where it develops enormously, both quantitatively and qualitatively.

paragraphs.source_en: The frequent contact of hunters with populations outside their territory is perceptible from the archaeological record in the form of raw material and pottery. Pastoral populations spread at around 7. 500 BP and they occupied the same territories as the hunter-gatherers. This coexistence, apparently peaceful, is visible from the archaeology and from the rock art. The onset of the desert conditions from around 3,000 BP must have been the definitive end of the Round Head art. These hunter-gatherers had to deal with a new climate and new social relations. They might have adopted the pastoral economy from their neighbours or they might have migrated towards the Sub-Saharan Africa where their culture continued.
